result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would make high-quality education universal—specifically education that teaches critical thinking, scientific literacy, emotional intelligence, and civic responsibility.

Why: these skills help people evaluate information, solve problems, cooperate across differences, and participate in democratic life. Effects would cascade: better public health decisions, more effective climate and economic policies, reduced susceptibility to misinformation and demagogues, and stronger social trust. Educated people are also better able to lift themselves out of poverty and innovate, so this change would shrink inequality while expanding opportunity.

It’s not a quick fix, but shifting the baseline of what everyone knows and how they think would transform nearly every other global challenge.
